meta.description: Yasakia is the dating app where you talk first: an AI agent gets to know you, then opens a small batch of people who fit you both ways. In construction.

chrome.footer: Yasakia is an open-source product by Krizaka, made in Québec.

status.label: Under development
status.text: Yasakia is being built in the open. There is no app to download and no account to create yet — this site says what it will be and shows what already runs.

home.title: Talk first. Meet both ways.
home.eyebrow: The dating app where you talk first
home.lead: No swipe, no catalogue, no score. An agent gets to know you in your own words, then opens a small batch of people who fit you in both directions.
home.principlesLead: What Yasakia refuses is as important as what it does.

talk.title: A conversation, not a form
talk.text: The agent asks one question at a time, with humour, in your language.

batch.title: Three to five people, not a feed
batch.text: A small batch, each with why you two in words — never a score.

both.title: Both ways, or not at all
both.text: Someone appears only if you fit them and they fit you.

debrief.title: The next batch waits for you
debrief.text: You debrief the last one first, so every batch fits better than the one before.

home.closingLead: Yasakia is open source, on the same foundations as Orochia and Orazaka. Read the code, or tell us what you expect from a dating app.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: The whole loop, from the first question to the first message — what the app is built to do.

talk.title: 1 · You talk
talk.text: An AI agent gets to know you, one question at a time, in your language. It runs on Orazaka, Krizaka's sovereign AI.

batch.title: 2 · A small batch opens
batch.text: Three to five people, never a catalogue. Each comes with the reasons you two fit, written in words.

both.title: 3 · It goes both ways
both.text: Filters and fit are checked in both directions: nobody is shown to someone who would not be shown to them.

debrief.title: 4 · You debrief
debrief.text: Tell the agent what you thought of the batch. The next one waits for that debrief, and fits better.

privacy.position: Your position is rounded to about one kilometre before it is stored.
privacy.photos: Photos are re-encoded to strip every metadata block, GPS included, and shown only to someone in your batch or your intro, through a link that expires in minutes.
privacy.encrypted: Sensitive answers are encrypted at rest.
privacy.control: Export and deletion of your data are in the API from day one; blocks and reports work at once.
privacy.honest: No demo mode and no fake profile: where there is nothing real, nothing is shown.

how.stackLead: One database does the heavy lifting; no broker, no swipe engine.

stack.db: PostgreSQL with pgvector for who you are and who you seek, and the radius.
stack.ui: Krizaka UI, web and native — the same components as the other Krizaka products.
stack.ai: Orazaka for the agent; it never leaves Krizaka's own stack.

demo.title: Demo
demo.lead: The app is not released. This is the one recording that exists: Krizaka UI's native components, the bricks Yasakia's screens are built from, running on a phone.
demo.videoLabel: A phone running Krizaka UI native components: a card deck, a tag selector and a location picker.
demo.note: It is a component demo, not the app. The portrait is generated for the demo — it is not a person and Yasakia has no members. The deck shown here is a building block; Yasakia itself has no swipe.
demo.nextText: Its own recording, made on the real application, replaces this one here. Until then: the code is public.
